The register is four people, a filing system and a legal fiction that has outlived three
co-op boards. It certifies soak tolerance and perfluorocarbon tolerance separately, inspects
nothing it is not invited to inspect, and withdraws certificates on paper evidence alone -
which is to say on the slot board, the charge logs and the indemnity notices, all of which the
co-op is obliged to post and all of which the clerk reads every shift.

Its internal split is the clerk. She is a register officer and a co-op member with a vote and
a pension in the fund, and every withdrawal she files costs somebody in the gallery a
certificate and costs the co-op a descent. The register's officers off-shelf have twice
proposed replacing her with an outsider. The co-op has twice made it clear what an outsider
would be shown.

Nobody at Kestrel loves the register. Everybody who has been down twice is alive because of
it.
